eyebrow: Lesson 14 · B1 · Being a Good Guest · 20 câu
heading: Arriving the Right Way
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Being a Good Guest – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 8–11.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Being a Good Guest (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: The moment you step through a friend's front door, your manners are on show. First, take off your hat, even if your hair is {sticking up|sticking up} in every direction underneath. It is a small but important sign of {respect|respect}.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Next, take off your shoes and leave them neatly on the {doormat|doormat}. This is especially important on snowy or rainy days. Nobody wants {muddy|muddy} footprints or {slushy|slushy} puddles all over their clean floors.

paras.label: C
paras.text: In Japan, taking off your shoes is a firm tradition. People remove them just inside the front door, and the host usually leaves a pair of {slippers|slippers} there for each guest to wear around the house.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Good guests also avoid surprises. Always phone before you {drop in on|drop in on} a friend or {relative|relative}. Never just appear on someone's {doorstep|doorstep} with a suitcase! Your friend may already have other plans, and an unexpected visitor can be stressful.

paras.label: E
paras.text: When you are invited to stay, tell your friend what time you will arrive and when you will be going home. Then stick to it. A good guest does not {outstay their welcome|outstay their welcome} by staying as long as they please.

vocab.vi: ở lâu quá mức chủ nhà mong muốn

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that says your hair is no excuse to break a rule
items.why: Đoạn A: *even if your hair is sticking up…*

items.label: A paragraph that explains why the weather makes one rule more important
items.why: Đoạn B: *especially important on snowy or rainy days.*

items.label: A paragraph that describes a custom in another country
items.why: Đoạn C: phong tục ở Nhật Bản.

items.label: A paragraph that warns against arriving with a suitcase without warning
items.why: Đoạn D: *Never just appear… with a suitcase!*

items.label: A paragraph that advises you to say when you will leave
items.why: Đoạn E: *when you will be going home.*

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: Why does the writer mention hair in (A)?
options: to show you should take off your hat even if your hair looks messy
to suggest you should brush your hair before a visit
to explain why hats are fashionable
to say that messy hair is rude
questions.why: *take off your hat, even if your hair is sticking up…*

questions.q: The writer suggests keeping your shoes on when it is raining.
questions.why: Sai. Bỏ giày ra *especially important on snowy or rainy days.*

questions.q: What do hosts in Japan often leave by the front door?
options: a doormat with each guest's name
questions.why: *the host usually leaves a pair of slippers there for each guest.*

questions.q: According to (D), why should you phone before visiting?
options: Your friend may already have other plans.
Phone calls are cheaper than visits.
Your friend may want to meet you at the station.
It is the law in many countries.
questions.why: *Your friend may already have other plans.*

questions.q: A surprise visit can cause stress for the person you are visiting.
questions.why: Đúng. *an unexpected visitor can be stressful.*

questions.q: What is the main message of the whole text?
options: Think about your host's home and plans when you visit.
Always take your own slippers when you visit friends.
Japanese homes are cleaner than other homes.
questions.why: Cả bài: giữ sạch nhà chủ, gọi trước, hẹn giờ về → nghĩ cho chủ nhà.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: Which piece of advice is the child following?
options: taking off wet boots by the door
questions.why: Đoạn B: cởi giày, để ở thảm cạnh cửa.
questions.alt: A child in a woolly hat and scarf sits by a red front door pulling off wet boots next to a doormat, while a cat watches

questions.q: Why is this rule especially important in the picture?
options: The weather is cold and wet.
questions.why: Mũ len, khăn, vũng nước → trời tuyết/mưa: *especially important on snowy or rainy days.*
questions.alt: A child in a woolly hat and scarf sits by a red front door pulling off wet boots next to a doormat, while a cat watches

questions.q: What is the girl most likely doing?
options: arranging a time to visit someone
questions.why: Gọi điện + xem lịch → hẹn trước giờ đến (đoạn D–E).
questions.alt: A girl talks on the phone while looking at a calendar; a dog sleeps on the floor

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last winter my cousin Tom decided to visit Grandma without telling her. [1] When he knocked on the door, nobody answered. [2] Now Tom always phones before he visits. [3]
options: He thought it would be a lovely surprise.
Grandma was so happy that she had cleaned the whole house for him.
He took off his boots and put on his slippers in the garden.
That way, Grandma has time to get ready, and she always bakes his favourite cake.
Grandma had gone to stay with her sister for the weekend.

items.why: Giải thích vì sao Tom không báo trước.
Không ai mở cửa → bà đi vắng (*may already have other plans*).
Lợi ích của việc gọi trước.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *…even if your hair is sticking up* (A). Hair that is **sticking up** is…
options: pointing upwards in a messy way

questions.q: *Always phone before you drop in on a friend* (D). To **drop in on** someone means to…
options: visit them, often without a fixed plan

questions.q: *A good guest does not outstay their welcome* (E). To **outstay your welcome** means to…
options: stay longer than your host wants
questions.why: **Out-** (vượt quá) + **stay** → ở lâu hơn chủ nhà mong muốn.
